name: Enterprise Software Product and Provenance

AISMM-3.1.0.evidence: provider dossier repository files, release notes and migration filename

pendingNeighbours.reason: identifier-unassigned EM-TEC-01 candidate; product and build relations unapproved

constraintRules.text: WM-SFT-001 owns durable Software Product identity, classification, offering and licence context, support statement and support lifecycle only.

WM-SFT-001 requires removal of eight embedded bundles—release record, artifact integrity, build provenance, BOM document, dependency graph, deployed instance, hosting environment and effective configuration—and replacement by approved typed references.
AISMM 3.1.0 is ALIGN context keyed to product_id or model_instance_id and never a second Software Product master.

Every AISMM projection is classified as derived, carries derivedFrom owner references and derivation metadata, passes an owner-validation gate, and never copies HR, incident or dataset payloads; a projection without derivedFrom is defective.
WM-SFT-007 owns Component and Package; WM-SFT-008 owns Build, Release and Artifact; WM-SFT-009 owns Deployment occurrence.
WM-SFT-003 remains a pending Interface Contract neighbour; WM-SFT-001 does not own interface contracts.
WM-SFT-012 remains SBOM document master; Product, Component and SBOM are distinct identities and bindings cite the SBOM without copying it.
Artifact digest identifies released bytes and never substitutes for AISMM semantic fingerprint.
Regional, tenant and repeated deployment never fork Software Product identity.
Release and Deployment are distinct N-to-M records; every redeployment creates a new Deployment occurrence without creating a new Release.
A product support statement is not a deployed-runtime observation and cannot be inferred from deployment state.
Every WM-SFT-008 build input pins Source Repository, immutable RepositoryRevision and subpath where applicable; this rule remains non-executable until the relation is approved.
One Software Product may reference many Source Repositories and one repository may support many products without identity merging; this relation remains pending allocation and approval.
SaaS, library, on-premise, container and firmware delivery profiles share product identity while delivery-specific artifacts and deployments remain external.
A SaaS product without a distributable artifact uses an explicit no-artifact degradation profile and never fabricates a package.
A library delivery references package and release artifacts and does not create Deployment unless an actual runtime occurrence exists.
An on-premise delivery references distributable release artifacts and each customer installation is a separate Deployment occurrence.
A container delivery distinguishes image Artifact digest from running Deployment and from Product semantic fingerprint.
A firmware delivery distinguishes Product, device-bound Deployment and firmware Artifact or Release.
AISMM evidence is pinned to repository release 3.1.0; runtime compatibility is unproven and no 3.2.0 delta is asserted without evidence.
